title: "QL-fitted means and NB mid-P transport"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{QL-fitted means and NB mid-P transport}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

ComBat-refQL 0.2.0 fits raw counts with edgeR v4:

```r
edgeR::glmQLFit(dge, design, dispersion = NULL, robust = TRUE, legacy = FALSE)
```

TMMwsp normalization is calculated once. The full-rank design has one named
coefficient per batch and preserves the supplied group and covariates. For a
sample in a non-reference batch, only its batch indicators are changed to form
the reference counterfactual design. The QL fit coefficients and offsets define
the observed and counterfactual means.

The v4 pipeline estimates one global underlying negative-binomial dispersion.
That `nb_dispersion` is the only dispersion passed to `pnbinom()`, `dnbinom()`,
and `qnbinom()`. Genewise `ql_dispersion` and
`posterior_ql_dispersion` describe residual quasi-likelihood variability; they
do not define a count CDF and are never NB distribution parameters.

For observed count $y$, the deterministic mid-P probability is

$$u=F_{NB}(y-1;\mu_{obs},\phi_{NB})+
\tfrac12P_{NB}(Y=y;\mu_{obs},\phi_{NB}).$$

The adjusted count is the NB quantile under the counterfactual reference mean
and the same valid global NB dispersion. Observed zeros remain zero. Genes that
are all zero in any batch are unsupported and returned unchanged. Transport is
performed by non-reference batch and gene chunk; intermediate means are not
retained in the result.
